question_text: A 23-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for a runny nose, sneezing, and coughing that has persisted for a few months. He denies feeling weak or tired, but states that his symptoms have disrupted his every day life. The patient has no significant past medical history. He drinks alcohol occasionally on the weekends. His temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 124/88 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, respirations are 13/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam reveals a healthy young man who is repetitively blowing his nose. Percussion of his sinuses elicits no symptoms. Inspection of the patient's oropharynx is unremarkable. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
